# PortProtonQt — Nix flake

Пакетирует [PortProtonQt](https://git.linux-gaming.ru/Linux-Gaming/PortProtonQt)
через тот же `meson.build`, что и апстримные PKGBUILD/rpm-спеки. Исходники
берутся напрямую с Gitea (`git+https://git.linux-gaming.ru/…`), ревизия
пиннута в `flake.lock` (git-протокол работает, хотя веб-интерфейс закрыт
Anubis anti-bot защитой).

## Преимущества по сравнению с raw/steam-run вариантом

В `portprotonqt-nix/` лежит сторонняя реализация (dark_siders), которая тоже
использует `steam-run`. Наш флейк — тот же проверенный подход (FHS-слой через
`steam-run`), но без его недостатков:

- **NixOS-модуль** `programs.portprotonqt`: udev-правило + ядро `uinput`,
  группа `portprotonqt`, polkit-правило — всё «из коробки» (у них только
  ручные шаги);
- **два выхода**: `portprotonqt` (release) и `portprotonqt-devel`;
- **фиксы NixOS уже в апстриме** и проверяются на сборке/в `nix flake check`
  (см. ниже), а не пришиты патчем;
- **интерпретатор зафиксирован**: внутри песочницы `#!/usr/bin/env python3`
  резолвился бы в чужой FHS-python без PySide6, поэтому мы явно вызываем
  наш `pythonEnv` по absolute path (store смонтирован в песочницу) и
  дополняем PYTHONPATH только чистым пакетом приложения.

## Зачем вообще FHS / почему «32-bit glibc» не виноват

Движку PortProton нужен не «32-bit glibc как таковой», а **FHS-окружение**:
скачанные им бинарники Steam Runtime (pressure-vessel) и Wine/Proton —
обычные dynamically-linked executables с интерпретатором
`/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`, которого на NixOS нет (stub-ld). Поэтому
все игры падали с «NixOS cannot run dynamically linked executables», а
подсказка «Install or enable 32-bit glibc» — лишь эвристика отчёта
(проверяет наличие `/lib/ld-linux.so.2`, отсутствующего на NixOS всегда).

`steam-run` (buildFHSEnv на базе bubblewrap из nixpkgs) даёт движку именно
это: настоящие `/usr`, `/lib`, `/lib64` с glibc. Порядок диагностики и
известные ловушки — в `portprotonqt-nix/NIXOS_NOTES.md`.

## Сборка

- `portprotonqt` (он же `default`) — **release**, снапшот `main`.
- `portprotonqt-devel` — **devel**, `-Dnightly=true` (как ночные сборки у
  апстрима).

```sh
nix build .#portprotonqt        # release
nix build .#portprotonqt-devel  # devel
nix run .#portprotonqt
```

Сборка требует `unfree` (steam-run + unrar) — он уже включён во флейке:

```sh
nix build .#portprotonqt
```

Обновить снапшот источника:

```sh
nix flake update portprotonqt-src
```

## Проверки

`nix flake check` прогоняет smoke-тесты: убеждается, что обёртка зовёт
`steam-run` и прописывает PYTHONPATH, что апстримные NixOS-фиксы на месте
(`PORTPROTONQT_PYTHON` в движке, `pw_ancestor_pid` в `kill_portwine`,
`sys.executable` в `app.py`), что `/usr` переписан на `$out` в конфиге, что
движок синтаксически валиден, что CLI отдаёт справку и скомпилированные
python-модули (`orjson`) грузятся правильным интерпретатором.

## Установка в систему

```nix
# в системном flake.nix
inputs.portprotonqt.url = "path:/путь/к/этому/flake";

modules = [
  portprotonqt.nixosModules.default
  {
    programs.portprotonqt.enable = true;
    # programs.portprotonqt.variant = "devel";
    users.users.myuser.extraGroups = [ "portprotonqt" ];
  }
];
```

Модуль, помимо установки пакета:
- включает `uinput` (виртуальный геймпад) и udev-правило на `/dev/uinput`;
- заводит группу `portprotonqt`;
- повторяет апстримное polkit-правило (NetworkManager/udisks2 для группы).

Группе без геймпада/`--ppqtos` система работать не мешает — добавление в неё опционально.

## Что стоит знать

- Vulkan: `vk_gpu_info` и Qt RHI нужен `vulkan-loader` — на NixOS включите
  `hardware.graphics.enable = true;`.
- `--ppqtos`/геймпад работают только при членстве в группе `portprotonqt`
  (см. выше).
- AppImage-самообновление в собранной из исходников версии не имеет смысла.
- Порты не найдены / приложение сразу выходит — проверьте, что `start.sh` лежит в
  `$out/share/portproton/scripts/` (на NixOS апстримный путь `/usr` не существует,
  flake уже переписывает его на `$out`).
- Игра падает с `137`/убивается `kill_portwine` — guard `pw_ancestor_pid`
  уже в апстримном `main`; подробности — в `portprotonqt-nix/NIXOS_NOTES.md`.
- Вся программа работает внутри steam-run-песочницы: GUI видит store и хост-данные
  (`--bind /home /home`), но не хост-PATH как таковой — поэтому интерпретатор
  зашит абсолютным путём из store.

https://gitlab.com/dark_siders/portproto.readme_excerpt: # PortProtonQt for NixOS Nix-флейк, собирающий **PortProtonQt** — графический интерфейс (PySide6) для запуска и управления играми из PortProton, Steam, Epic Games Store и GOG. Собирается **из исходников апстрима** через Meson. AppImage не используется. ## Быстрый старт ```bash nix run gitlab:dark_siders/portprotonqt-nix ``` или из клона репозитория: ```bash nix run .#portproton ``` Сборка: ```bash nix build . ./result/bin/portprotonqt ``` ## Что внутри Весь пакет — один файл `flake.nix`. Отдельных derivation'ов, оверлеев и директорий `pkgs/` нет: пакет строится из входа `portprotonqt-src`, который тянет официальный репозиторий апстрима. | | | | --- | --- | | Источник | `git+https://git.linux-gaming.ru/Linux-Gaming/PortProtonQt`, ветка `main` | | Пин ревизии | `flake.lock` (`portprotonqt-src`) | | Сборка | Meson + Nix, версия `1.4.1` | | Python | `python313.withPackages` со всем набором зависимостей | | FHS-слой | `steam-run` | ## Версия Пакет собирается **с ветки `main`, а не с тега релиза**: версия в derivation — `1.4.1`, но исходники всегда свежие. Точная ревизия зафиксирована в `flake.lock`. Так NixOS-фиксы апстрима подхватываются сразу, без ожидания следующего релиза. ## Как это работает PortProtonQt — не только GUI. Он же тянет и запускает **bash-движок PortProton** (`start.sh`), который скачивает Wine/Proton и запускает игры. Этому движку нужна обычная FHS-система с glibc, bash и системными утилитами, чего в NixOS нет. Поэтому пакет запускается через **`steam-run`** — FHS-окружение на базе bubblewrap, уже присутствующее в nixpkgs. Ничего самодельного: своя FHS-сборка не нужна, `steam-run` умеет всё, что требуется. ## Правки для NixOS Апстрим NixOS не поддерживает официально. Две основные проблемы **уже исправлены в апстриме** (коммит `e25b52f3`), остаётся только строгая проверка в `postInstall`. 1. **Абсолютный интерпретатор в скриптах движка.** `steam-run` отдаёт в песочницу `PATH`, где `python3` — чужой интерпретатор из FHS-образа. Он подхватывает чистые модули вроде `babel`, но не грузит скомпилированные (`orjson`, `pyside6`) — несовпадает ABI-тег. **Исправлено апстримом**: `app.py` прописывает `PORTPROTONQT_PYTHON=sys.executable`, скрипты движка зовут `${PORTPROTONQT_PYTHON:-python3}`. 2. **Защита `kill_portwine`.** Функция ищет bwrap через `pgrep -f wrap | grep PortProton` и шлёт `kill -n 9`. Под `steam-run` этот bwrap — собственный контейнер сессии, а у него `--die-with-parent`, поэтому всё падало с SIGKILL (код 137) ещё до запуска игры. **Исправлено апстримом**: в `functions_helper` добавлен guard `pw_ancestor_pid`, отбрасывающий предков текущего шелла из списка на kill. 3. **Строгая проверка подмен** (в `postInstall`). Если апстрим переименует переменную `PORTPROTONQT_PYTHON` или уберёт guard `pw_ancestor_pid`, сборка упадёт с внятной ошибкой, а не сломается молча у пользователя. Никаких правок исходников на уровне Python — всё делается на уровне установленных скриптов. ## Проверки ```bash nix flake check ``` | атрибут | что проверяет | | --- | --- | | `package` | сама сборка | | `cli` | обёртка зовёт `steam-run` и прописывает `PYTHONPATH`; в скриптах движка нет голых вызовов `python3 -m portprotonqt`; на месте защита `kill_portwine`; `bash -n` сходит для обоих скриптов; CLI отдаёт справку; `orjson` и `babel` импортируются тем же интерпретатором, которым зовут хелперы движка | Быстрый прогон одного набора: ```bash nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.cli ``` ## Подключение в свой конфиг Через inputs (рекомендуется): ```nix { inputs = { portprotonqt-nix.url = "gitlab:dark_siders/portprotonqt-nix"; }; outputs = { nixpkgs, portprotonqt-nix, ... }: { nixosConfigurations.myhost = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem { system = "x86_64-linux"; modules = [ ({ modulesPath, ... }: { imports = [ (modulesPath + "/installer/scan/not-detected.nix") ]; nixpkgs.overlays = [ portprotonqt-nix.overlays.default ]; environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.portprotonqt ]; }) ]; }; }; } ``` Или напрямую во flake-конфиге: ```nix { inputs.portprotonqt-nix.url = "gitlab:dark_siders/portprotonqt-nix"; # ... nixpkgs.overlays = [ inputs.portprotonqt-nix.overlays.default ]; environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.portprotonqt ]; } ``` > **Примечание:** пакет зависит от `steam-run` (проприетарный), поэтому нужен > `nixpkgs.config.allowUnfree = true;` — во флейке он уже задан. ## Права для wine (polkit) — опционально Апстрим закрыл CVE-2026-59678 в 1.3.1: polkit-правило `ru.linux_gaming.PortProtonQt.rules` больше не полагается на проверку `ps`, а даёт привилегии только членам группы `portprotonqt`. На NixOS эта группа не создаётся системой автоматически. Если хотите разрешить бесшовное монтирование дисков и правку NetworkManager прямо из GUI, добавьте: ```nix users.groups.portprotonqt = { }; users.users.YOUR_USER.extraGroups = [ "portprotonqt" ]; ``` Без этого polkit-правило просто не сработает (безопасный дефолт) — приложение продолжит работать. ## Ограничения - Только `x86_64-linux`: `steam-run` под другие системы не собирается. - Первая инициализация Wine/Proton заметно дольше обычного: движок качает дистрибутивы и компилирует модули уже внутри FHS-окружения. - Пакет тянет ветку `main` апстрима, а не тег: возможны сюрпризы при обновлении `flake.lock`. Фиксированная ревизия всегда в `flake.lock`. - `gogdl` (GOG) и `legendary` (Epic) в замыкание не входят, но ставить их в систему не нужно: сам PortProtonQt скачивает их из официальных релизов Heroic в `~/.local/share/PortProtonQt/bin` (со сверкой sha256) и обновляет раз в 30 дней. Из `PATH` они берутся только если своего бинаря нет. - Путь к данным PortProton задаётся в GUI или через `PORT_DATA_PATH`. В флейк никакие личные пути не зашиты. - `meta.maintainers` пуст — для попадания в nixpkgs нужно завести maintainer. ## Лицензия Nix-выражения флейка — MIT. Сам **PortProtonQt** распространяется под лицензией **GPL-3.0**.

# Proton Mail Bridge
Copyright (c) 2026 Proton AG

This repository holds the Proton Mail Bridge application.
For a detailed build information see [BUILDS](./BUILDS.md).
The license can be found in [LICENSE](./LICENSE) file, for more licensing information see [COPYING_NOTES](./COPYING_NOTES.md).
For contribution policy see [CONTRIBUTING](./CONTRIBUTING.md).


## Description Bridge
Proton Mail Bridge for e-mail clients.

When launched, Bridge will initialize local IMAP/SMTP servers and render 
its GUI.

To configure an e-mail client, first log in using your Proton Mail credentials. 
Open your e-mail client and add a new account using the settings which are 
located in the Bridge GUI. The client will only be able to sync with 
your Proton Mail account when the Bridge is running, thus the option 
to start Bridge on startup is enabled by default.

When the main window is closed, Bridge will continue to run in the
background.

More details [on the public website](https://proton.me/mail/bridge).

## Launcher
The launcher is a binary used to run the Proton Mail Bridge.

The Official distribution of the Proton Mail Bridge application contains
both a launcher and the app itself. The launcher is installed in a protected
area of the system (i.e. an area accessible only with admin privileges) and is
used to run the app. The launcher ensures that nobody tampered with the app's
files by verifying their signature using a hardcoded public key. App files are
placed in regular userspace and are signed by Proton's private key. This
feature enables the app to securely update itself automatically without asking
the user for a password.

## Keychain
You need to have a keychain in order to run Proton Mail Bridge. On Mac or
Windows, Bridge uses native credential managers. On Linux, use `secret-service` freedesktop.org API
(e.g. [Gnome keyring](https://wiki.gnome.org/Projects/GnomeKeyring/))
or
[pass](https://www.passwordstore.org/). We are working on allowing other secret
services (e.g. KeepassXC), but for now only gnome-keyring is usable without
major problems.


## Environment Variables

### Dev build or run
- `APP_VERSION`: set the bridge app version used during testing or building
- `PROTONMAIL_ENV`: when set to `dev` it is not using Sentry to report crashes
- `VERBOSITY`: set log level used during test time and by the makefile

### Integration testing
- `TEST_ENV`: set which env to use (fake or live)
- `TEST_ACCOUNTS`: set JSON file with configured accounts
- `TAGS`: set build tags for tests
- `FEATURES`: set feature dir, file or scenario to test

## Folders

There are now three types of system folders which Bridge recognises:

|        | Windows                             | Mac                                                 | Linux                               | Linux (XDG)                           |
|--------|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| config | %APPDATA%\protonmail\bridge-v3      | ~/Library/Application Support/protonmail/bridge-v3  | ~/.config/protonmail/bridge-v3      | $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/protonmail/bridge-v3 |
| cache  | %LOCALAPPDATA%\protonmail\bridge-v3 | ~/Library/Caches/protonmail/bridge-v3               | ~/.cache/protonmail/bridge-v3       | $XDG_CACHE_HOME/protonmail/bridge-v3  |
| data	  | %APPDATA%\protonmail\bridge-v3      | ~/Library/Application Support/protonmail/bridge-v3  | ~/.local/share/protonmail/bridge-v3 | $XDG_DATA_HOME/protonmail/bridge-v3   |
| temp   | %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp                 | $TMPDIR if non-empty, else /tmp                     | $TMPDIR if non-empty, else /tmp     | $TMPDIR if non-empty, else /tmp       |

Introduction
------------

**Proton** is a tool for use with the Steam client which allows games which are
exclusive to Windows to run on the Linux operating system. It uses Wine to
facilitate this.

**Most users should use Proton provided by the Steam Client itself.** See
[this Steam Community post][steam-play-introduction] for more details.

The source code is provided to enable advanced users the ability to alter
Proton. For example, some users may wish to use a different version of Wine
with a particular title.

**The changelog** is available on [our wiki][changelog].

[steam-play-introduction]: https://steamcommunity.com/games/221410/announcements/detail/1696055855739350561
[changelog]: https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton/wiki/Changelog


Obtaining Proton sources
------------------------

Acquire Proton's source by cloning <https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton>
and checking out the branch you desire.

You can clone the latest Proton to your system with this command:

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton.git proton
```

Be sure to update submodules when switching between branches:

```bash
git checkout experimental_6.3
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

If you want to change any subcomponent, now is the time to do so. For
example, if you wish to make changes to Wine, you would apply them to the
`wine/` directory.


Building Proton
---------------

Most of Proton builds inside the Proton SDK container with very few
dependencies on the host side.

## Preparing the build environment

You need either a Docker or a Podman setup. We highly recommend [the rootless
Podman setup][rootless-podman]. Please refer to your distribution's
documentation for setup instructions (e.g. Arch [Podman][arch-podman] /
[Docker][arch-docker], Debian [Podman][debian-podman] /
[Docker][debian-docker]).

[rootless-podman]: https://github.com/containers/podman/blob/main/docs/tutorials/rootless_tutorial.md
[arch-podman]: https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Podman
[arch-docker]: https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Docker
[debian-podman]: https://wiki.debian.org/Podman
[debian-docker]: https://wiki.debian.org/Docker


## The Easy Way

We provide a top-level Makefile which will execute most of the build commands
for you.

After checking out the repository and updating its submodules, assuming that
you have a working Docker or Podman setup, you can build and install Proton
with a simple:

```bash
make install
```

If your build system is missing dependencies, it will fail quickly with a clear
error message.

After the build finishes, you may need to restart the Steam client to see the
new Proton tool. The tool's name in the Steam client will be based on the
currently checked out branch of Proton. You can override this name using the
`build_name` variable.

See `make help` for other build targets and options.



## Manual building

### Configuring the build

```bash
mkdir ../build && cd ../build
../proton/configure.sh --enable-ccache --build-name=my_build
```

Running `configure.sh` will create a `Makefile` allowing you to build Proton.
The scripts checks if containers are functional and prompt you if any
host-side dependencies are missing. You should run the command from a
directory created specifically for your build.

The configuration script tries to discover a working Docker or Podman setup
to use, but you can force a compatible engine with
`--container-engine=<executable_name>`.

You can enable ccache with `--enable-cache` flag. This will mount your
`$CCACHE_DIR` or `$HOME/.ccache` inside the container.

`--proton-sdk-image=registry.gitlab.steamos.cloud/proton/soldier/sdk:<version>`
can be used to build with a custom version of the Proton SDK images.

Check `--help` for other configuration options.

NOTE: If **SELinux** is in use, the Proton build container may fail to access
your user's files. This is caused by [SELinux's filesystem
labels][selinux-labels]. You may pass the `--relabel-volumes` switch to
configure to cause the [container engine to relabel its
bind-mounts][bind-mounts] and allow access to those files from within the
container. This can be dangerous when used with system directories. Proceed
with caution and refer your container engine's manual.

[selinux-labels]: https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/6/html/security-enhanced_linux/sect-security-enhanced_linux-working_with_selinux-selinux_contexts_labeling_files
[bind-mounts]: https://docs.docker.com/storage/bind-mounts/


### Building

```
make
```

**Important make targets:**

`make install` - install Proton into your user's Steam directory, see the [install Proton
locally](#install-proton-locally) section for details.

`make redist` - create a redistribute build (`redist/`) that can be copied to
`~/.steam/root/compatibilitytools.d/`.

`make deploy` - create a deployment build (`deploy/`). This is what we use to
deploy Proton to Steam users via Steamworks.

`make module=<module> module` - build both 32- and 64-bit versions of the
specified wine module. This allows rapid iteration on one module. This target
is only useful after building Proton.

`make dxvk` / `make vkd3d-proton` - rebuild DXVK / vkd3d-proton.


### Debug Builds

To prevent symbol stripping add `UNSTRIPPED_BUILD=1` to the `make`
invocation. This should be used only with a clean build directory.

E.g.:

```
mkdir ../debug-proton-build && cd ../debug-proton-build
../proton/configure.sh --enable-ccache --build-name=debug_build
make UNSTRIPPED_BUILD=1 install
```


Install Proton locally
----------------------

Steam ships with several versions of Proton, which games will use by default or
that you can select in Steam Settings' Steam Play page. Steam also supports
running games with local builds of Proton, which you can install on your
machine.

To install a local build of Proton into Steam, make a new directory in
`~/.steam/root/compatibilitytools.d/` with a tool name of your choosing and
place the directory containing your redistributable build under that path.

The `make install` target will perform this task for you, installing the
Proton build into the Steam folder for the current user. You will have to
restart the Steam client for it to pick up on a new tool.

A correct local tool installation should look similar to this:

```
compatibilitytools.d/my_proton/
├── compatibilitytool.vdf
├── filelock.py
├── LICENSE
├── proton
├── proton_dist.tar
├── toolmanifest.vdf
├── user_settings.sample.py
└── version
```

To enable your local build in Steam, go to the Steam Play section of the
Settings window. If the build was correctly installed, you should see
"proton-localbuild" in the drop-down list of compatibility tools.

Each component of this software is used under the terms of their licenses.
See the `LICENSE` files here, as well as the `LICENSE`, `COPYING`, etc files
in each submodule and directory for details. If you distribute a built
version of Proton to other users, you must adhere to the terms of these
licenses.


Debugging
---------

Proton builds have their symbols stripped by default. You can switch to
"debug" beta branch in Steam (search for Proton in your library,
Properties... -> BETAS -> select "debug") or build without stripping (see
[Debug Builds section](#debug-builds)).

The symbols are provided through the accompanying `.debug` files which may
need to be explicitly loaded by the debugging tools. For GDB there's a helper
script `wine/tools/gdbinit.py` (source it) that provides `load-symbol-files`
(or `lsf` for short) command which loads the symbols for all the mapped files.

For tips on debugging see [docs/DEBUGGING.md](docs/DEBUGGING.md).


`compile_commands.json`
-----------------------

For use with [clangd](https://clangd.llvm.org/) LSP server and similar tooling.

Projects built using cmake or meson (e.g. vkd3d-proton) automatically come with
`compile_commands.json`. For autotools (e.g. wine) you have to [configure the
build](#configuring-the-build) with `--enable-bear` that uses
[bear](https://github.com/rizsotto/Bear) to create the compilation database.
It's not on by default as it make the build slightly slower.

The build system collects all the created compile_commands.json files in a
build subdirectory named `compile_commands/`.

The paths are translated to point to the real source (i.e. not the rsynced
copy). It still may depend on build directory for things like auto-generated
`config.h` though and for wine it may be beneficial to run `tools/make_requests`
in you source directories as those changes are not committed.

You can then configure your editor to use that file for clangd in a few ways:

1) directly - some editors/plugins allow you to specify the path to `compile_commands.json`
2) via `.clangd` file, e.g.
```bash
cd src/proton/wine/
cat > .clangd <<EOF
CompileFlags:
  CompilationDatabase: ../build/current-dev/compile_commands/wine64/
EOF
```
3) by symlinking:
```bash
ln -s ../build/current-dev/compile_commands/wine64/compile_commands.json .
```


Runtime Config Options
----------------------

Proton can be tuned at runtime to help certain games run. The Steam client sets
some options for known games using the `STEAM_COMPAT_CONFIG` variable.
You can override these options using the environment variables described below.

The best way to set these environment overrides for all games is by renaming
`user_settings.sample.py` to `user_settings.py` and modifying it appropriately.
This file is located in the Proton installation directory in your Steam library
(often `~/.steam/steam/steamapps/common/Proton #.#`).

If you want to change the runtime configuration for a specific game, you can
use the `Set Launch Options` setting in the game's `Properties` dialog in the
Steam client. Set the variable, followed by `%command%`. For example, input
"`PROTON_USE_WINED3D=1 %command%`" to use the OpenGL-based wined3d renderer
instead of the Vulkan-based DXVK renderer.

To enable an option, set the variable to a non-`0` value.  To disable an
option, set the variable to `0`. To use Steam's default configuration, do
not specify the variable at all.

the Wine prefix. Removing the option will revert to the previous behavior.

https://gitlab.com/see-honden/lumo-expor.readme_excerpt:
# Lumo Export

Export your [Proton Lumo](https://lumo.proton.me) conversations: one chat at a time, or **every chat
in a single batch**.

Lumo has no built-in export. This extension reads the chat pages inside your own browser, formats
them, and writes them to disk. Nothing is uploaded anywhere, there is no server, and there is no
telemetry.

- **Single chat:** pick individual messages, choose Markdown (preselected) / JSON / plain text / HTML / Base64,
  optionally AES-256 encrypt the result, extract code blocks, extract generated images, export saved
  memories, or use find & replace to anonymise text before saving.
- **Batch:** walk your whole chat list and save all conversations at once as one ZIP archive,
  individual files, or a single combined document — already sorted into `Projects/<project>/`,
  `Favorites/` and `General/`, with live progress, per-chat retry, and partial saving if you stop
  early.

Two ways to install it: the **packaged install** (one command, no clone, verified download) or
**developer mode from a checkout** if you want to work on the code. Both end with the same step: a
folder loaded as an unpacked extension.

---

## Install (packaged, recommended)

Every push to `main` builds a package, and a push that bumps the extension version publishes it as a
release, so there is nothing to clone. The package the installer downloads always comes from the tip
of `main`, even between releases.

### One-line installer

```bash
curl -fsSL https://gitlab.com/see-honden/lumo-export/-/raw/main/install.sh | bash
```

The script downloads the package built from `main`, verifies its SHA-256 against the published
`checksums.txt`, and unpacks it into `~/.local/share/lumo-export/extension` (override with
`LUMO_EXPORT_DIR=/somewhere/else`). It aborts without installing anything if the checksum does not
match.

### Load the folder (once)

1. Open `brave://extensions` (Chromium: `chrome://extensions`, Edge: `edge://extensions`)
2. Turn on **Developer mode** (top-right toggle)
3. Click **Load unpacked** and select the folder the installer printed
4. Click the puzzle-piece icon in the toolbar and pin **Lumo Chat Export**

Brave shows *"This extension is not from the Chrome Web Store"* — expected for unpacked extensions
and not a problem.

### Manual download instead

1. Open the [releases page](https://gitlab.com/see-honden/lumo-export/-/releases) and download
   `lumo-export-chromium-v<version>.zip` and `checksums.txt`
2. Verify: `sha256sum -c checksums.txt`
3. Unpack it anywhere and load that folder as described above

### Updating a packaged install

Re-run the installer, then click the **↻ reload** button on the extension card in
`brave://extensions`. Chromium only auto-updates extensions installed from a store or by policy, so
an unpacked extension needs that one click (a self-hosted update manifest is on the roadmap).

---

## Install (developer mode, from a checkout)

Use this if you want to modify the extension or run the test suites. The extension folder is
[`chromium/`](chromium/) in this repository.

### 1. Get the source

```bash
git clone git@gitlab.com:see-honden/lumo-export.git
cd lumo-export
```

Or download the repository as a ZIP and unpack it. Note the full path of the `chromium/` folder
inside it, e.g. `~/src/lumo-export/chromium`.

### 2. Load it unpacked

**Brave**

1. Open a new tab and go to `brave://extensions`
2. Turn on **Developer mode** (top-right toggle)
3. Click **Load unpacked**
4. Select the `chromium/` folder from step 1
5. Brave shows *"This extension is not from the Chrome Web Store"* — that is expected for unpacked
   extensions and does not indicate a problem
6. Click the puzzle-piece icon in the toolbar, then the pin next to **Lumo Chat Export** so the icon
   stays visible

**Chrome / Chromium**

Identical, with `chrome://extensions` as the start page.

**Edge**

Identical, with `edge://extensions` as the start page.

### 3. Verify it works

1. Open `https://lumo.proton.me` in a tab and sign in (guest chats have no history to export).
2. Click the **Lumo Chat Export** icon. The popup should list the messages of the chat you are
   looking at. If it says *"No messages found"*, make sure the Lumo tab is the active tab and that
   the chat has finished loading.
3. Sanity check the build: **🛡️ Security** → **Verify Code Integrity**. On a clean checkout this
   reports *"Code Integrity Verified"* with the SHA-256 of `chromium/popup.js`.

### 4. Updating

```bash
cd lumo-export && git pull
```

Then go back to `brave://extensions` (or `chrome://extensions`) and click the **↻ reload** button on
the Lumo Chat Export card. The extension picks up the new files immediately.

Do not move or rename the folder after installing: the browser stores the path, and a moved folder
shows up as *"Manifest file is missing or unreadable"*. The fix is **Remove**, then **Load unpacked**
again from the new location.

### 5. Uninstalling

`brave://extensions` → **Lumo Chat Export** → **Remove**. Nothing else is left behind: the extension
only stores your own settings in the browser's extension storage.

---

## Using it

### Single chat

Open the chat in Lumo, click the extension icon, select the messages you want (or **All**), pick a
format, and press **Export Selected**. Markdown is preselected; every other format stays one click
away, and a format you picked in the batch page is remembered there.

| Feature | Notes |
|---|---|
| Formats | Markdown (default, keeps code blocks), JSON (structured), plain text, HTML, Base64 |
| Encryption | AES-256-GCM with PBKDF2 (100k iterations); output is a `.json.enc` bundle |
| Find & replace | Comma-separated find/replace pairs, applied during export only |
| Every fork | *Include every conversation fork* is built but **disabled in this release**: the branch walk is still being validated against Lumo's current markup, so a forked chat is saved as a single file for now |
| Code blocks / images | Scan the chat and export only the code snippets or generated images |
| Memory export | Exports saved Lumo memories as JSON (opens Settings → Memory automatically) |
| Search & tooltips | Live filtered list with highlighted matches, no need to open messages |

### Batch export: all conversations at once

1. Open Lumo and sign in.
2. In the popup, click **📚 Batch Export (all chats)**. The batch page opens in a normal tab, so a
   long export is never cut short by the popup closing.
3. Click **🔍 Scan my conversations**. The extension reads three places in your account, in order:
   the **All chats** view (the full list; it is virtualized, so it scrolls through it), the
   **projects overview** (`/u/<session>/projects`, for project names), and then **each project's own
   page** for its chat list. The result is one list where every chat shows its placement.
4. Choose a format and a delivery mode:

   | Delivery | Result |
   |---|---|
   | One ZIP archive (default) | `lumo-export-YYYY-MM-DD.zip` containing `<nnn>-<title>-<id>.<ext>` files inside `Projects/<project>/`, `Favorites/` and `General/`, plus an `index.json` manifest that records each chat's placement |
   | Individual files | One download per placement into `Downloads/lumo-export-YYYY-MM-DD/<placement>/` |
   | One combined file | A single document grouped into project, favorites and general sections in that order |

   **Fork export is not available in this release.** The option exists in both pages, disabled, and
   the walk behind it is implemented and unit-tested, but it has not been confirmed against the live
   Lumo page: an edited user message keeps its sibling switcher in a different place than an answer,
   and the chevrons carry no label the extension can match on. Until that is validated, every chat —
   forked or not — is saved as a single file using the branch that is on screen, exactly as before.

5. Click **⬇️ Download all conversations**. Progress, per-chat status, and errors are shown live.

**Where a chat ends up:** a chat that lives in a project goes under `Projects/<project>/`; a
favorited chat goes under `Favorites/`; everything else goes under `General/`. A chat that is both
favorited *and* in a project is saved twice, once in each folder, with identical content — it is
still read from the tab only once. Project membership comes from the chat list row and from the
project's own page, so a chat is placed in its project even when its row does not say so. Anything
that cannot be attributed is reported in the run log and placed in `General/` rather than dropped,
and a project without chats is reported instead of creating an empty folder.

Batch options: embed generated images (larger files), find & replace before saving, stop after the current chat
(**Stop**, then **Save what we have** to keep what was already read), **Retry failed** without
re-reading the chats that worked, *Use a separate Lumo tab* to keep your own tab where it is, and
*Return to the chat I was reading* to jump back when finished.

Encryption in batch mode produces one `lumo-export-YYYY-MM-DD.json.enc` bundle with every
conversation. It uses the same container format as the single-chat encryption (salt + IV +
AES-GCM ciphertext), so the standalone Python decryptor in [`firefox/decrypt/`](firefox/decrypt/)
can open it. The bundle's payload carries each chat's project and favorite state, so no structure
is lost in the encrypted mode.

Batch export navigates your Lumo tab through each conversation. That is how the Lumo web app loads
history: there is no public API to read a chat without rendering it. Scanning costs one page load
per project on top of the chat list; each project is named in the run log while it is read.

---

## Privacy

The extension reads the chat pages inside your own browser and writes files to your disk. It has no
server, no account, no cloud component and no telemetry, and it sends nothing anywhere. The only
network traffic an export causes is the page loads it performs in your own signed-in Lumo tab.

That guarantee is enforced rather than promised: `npm run test:unit` runs a **Local-only guarantee**
section in `tests/selftest.js` that fails if an extension script ships an XHR/WebSocket/beacon
client, if a `fetch` reads anything other than one of the extension's own files, if a script names a
host other than `lumo.proton.me`, or if the manifest asks for any permission beyond `downloads`,
`scripting` and `storage` with host access to `https://lumo.proton.me/*`. `npm run test:batch`
additionally asserts that an encryption passphrase is used for one run and never written to storage.
For that reason there is no privacy notice inside the extension UI: the claim lives in the
repository and in the tests, where it can be checked.

---

## Repository layout

```
chromium/            the extension you load unpacked
  manifest.json      Manifest V3; content_scripts.js is the content-script load order
  core/namespace.js  the one Lumo namespace every module hangs its API off
  domain/            pure policy: messages, forks, naming, placements, packaging, discovery,
                     formats, find & replace, run report
  ports/             the seams: chat-tree, lumo-page, downloads, settings, archive, crypto, clock
  adapters/          one implementation per external system: the Lumo DOM page, the sibling
                     switcher, the remote page, chrome platform/downloads/storage, WebCrypto,
                     the ZIP writer, the clock
  app/               use cases: read a conversation, scan the account, package an export,
                     export one chat
  content.js         the page-side composition root: builds the adapters, routes messages
  popup.*            the single-chat UI
  batch.*            the batch UI and its run loop
firefox/             unmodified upstream Firefox edition, kept as a reference
tests/               dependency-free + jsdom test suites
scripts/build.sh     builds dist/ (versioned ZIP, stable alias, checksums, version.env)
scripts/z

import setuptools
import os
import codecs


def read(rel_path):
    here = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(__file__))
    # intentionally *not* adding an encoding option to open, See:
    #   https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/issues/201#issuecomment-3145690
    with codecs.open(os.path.join(here, rel_path), 'r') as fp:
        return fp.read()


def get_version(rel_path):
    for line in read(rel_path).splitlines():
        if line.startswith('__version__'):
            # __version__ = "0.9"
            delim = '"' if '"' in line else "'"
            return line.split(delim)[1]
    raise RuntimeError("Unable to find version string.")


long_description = read("README.md")

setuptools.setup(
    name="Proton",
    version=get_version(os.path.join('Proton', '__init__.py')),
    author="Bolun.Han",
    author_email="Bolun.Han@outlook.com",
    description="HFT Factor Mining Platform",
    long_description=long_description,
    long_description_content_type="text/markdown",
    url="https://github.com/BolunHan/Proton",
    packages=setuptools.find_packages(),
    include_package_data=True,
    package_data={
    },

A two-way sync tool for Proton Drive on Pop!OS Linux.

**Status**: Phase 2 - File Watching ✅ COMPLETE

**Architecture**: This project now uses a **backend abstraction layer** with `rclone` as the default provider and a gated `sdk` provider for incremental Proton Drive SDK integration.

https://gitlab.com/gabriel17166/arrpc-pe.readme_excerpt:
# arRPC Personalizado Pessoal Linux

Meu Rich Presence caseiro para o Discord no Linux — feito porque o Discord
ignora metade do que eu uso: jogo nativo, jogo sob Proton, série no Stremio,
música e vídeo no navegador. Em vez de esperar suporte, o daemon procura os
processos e **fala o protocolo IPC do Discord direto**.

Python puro (só biblioteca padrão), roda como serviço systemd de usuário e
sobe sozinho no boot. Sem Node, sem arRPC oficial, sem plugin do Vencord.

Vem com um **ícone de bandeja** (GTK3 + AppIndicator, nada de Qt e nenhuma
janela): tudo — quais apps o Discord enxerga, aparência do ícone, início
automático — se resolve pelo menu.

---

## O problema

O Discord detecta jogos comparando os processos abertos com a base pública de
jogos detectáveis (`https://discord.com/api/v9/applications/detectable`). No
Linux essa base falha de várias formas ao mesmo tempo:

| Situação | O que a base traz | Resultado |
|---|---|---|
| RuneScape nativo (`rs2client`) | só executáveis `win32` e `darwin` | nunca detecta |
| GTA SA sob Proton (`gta-sa.exe`) | executável `win32` | o processo tem caminho Wine, não bate |
| TBH: Task Bar Hero | **nenhum** executável cadastrado | nunca detecta |
| Stremio, YouTube, YouTube Music | não existem na base | nunca detecta |

Este projeto resolve pelo outro lado: eu digo qual processo é qual app, e o
daemon publica a presença.

## O que ele mostra

| App | Como detecta | O que aparece |
|---|---|---|
| **RuneScape 3** | processo `rs2client` | "Gielinor" |
| **Minecraft** (Prism) | processo da instância | instância, **servidor conectado** e **lotação** (ex.: `860 of 5000`) |
| **Left 4 Dead 2** | `hl2_linux` ou `.exe` no Proton | **campanha e capítulo** ("Dark Carnival — capítulo 3") |
| **GTA: San Andreas** | memória do processo | **bairro, veículo, vida, dinheiro**, estrelas de procurado e "Em missão" |
| **TBH: Task Bar Hero** | `TaskBarHero.exe` sob Proton | "Jogando" |
| **Stremio** | MPRIS | **série — episódio** ("Prison Break — Unearthed (2x9)") |
| **YouTube** (Firefox) | MPRIS + URL da aba | **título e canal**, miniatura do vídeo, progresso, botão do vídeo |
| **YouTube Music** (Firefox) | MPRIS + URL da aba | **faixa — artista**, capa do álbum, progresso, botões |
| **Claude Code** | nome do executável | "Programming" e o tempo de sessão — nada além disso |

Adicionar um app novo é escolher no menu da bandeja, ou editar um JSON —
nenhuma linha de código. Veja [O ícone de bandeja](#o-ícone-de-bandeja) e
[Adicionar seus próprios apps](#adicionar-seus-próprios-apps).

---

## Instalação

### Pacote pronto

Baixe da [página de releases](https://github.com/gabrielmf1998/Discord-Arrpc-Detector-KDE/releases):

| Distro | Arquivo | Comando |
|---|---|---|
| **Fedora**, RHEL, Nobara | `.rpm` | `sudo dnf install ./discord-game-presence-*.noarch.rpm` |
| **Debian**, Ubuntu, Mint, Pop!_OS | `.deb` | `sudo apt install ./discord-game-presence_*_all.deb` |
| **Arch**, Manjaro, EndeavourOS, CachyOS | `.pkg.tar.zst` | `sudo pacman -U ./discord-game-presence-*-any.pkg.tar.zst` |
| Qualquer outra | `.AppImage` | `chmod +x DiscordPresence-*.AppImage && ./DiscordPresence-*.AppImage` |

Depois, uma vez, sem root:

```bash
systemctl --user enable --now discord-game-presence.service
systemctl --user enable --now discord-game-presence-tray.service
```

Arch também pode construir do jeito idiomático com o
[`PKGBUILD`](packaging/arch/PKGBUILD) do repositório.

O `.AppImage` carrega o código do projeto mas usa o **Python e o GTK do
sistema** — empacotar GTK inteiro passaria de 100 MB e ainda quebraria a
integração com o tema de ícones do desktop, que é justamente o que a bandeja
usa. Ele aceita `./DiscordPresence-*.AppImage daemon` para rodar só o daemon e
`install` para copiar tudo para `~/.local/bin`.

### Script (instala também o Vesktop)

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabrielmf1998/Discord-Arrpc-Detector-KDE/main/install.sh | bash
```

O instalador:

1. detecta a distro (Arch, Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora, openSUSE, ou genérica);
2. instala as dependências (`python3`, `iproute2`/`ss`, `curl`);
3. instala o **Vesktop nativo** — pacote do repositório no Arch, `.deb`/`.rpm`
   oficial nas demais, tarball em `/opt` como reserva;
4. instala o daemon em `~/.local/bin` e o serviço em `~/.config/systemd/user`,
   já habilitado;
5. liga o log de console do L4D2, necessário para saber o mapa.

Já usa outro cliente que exponha o socket de IPC? `SKIP_VESKTOP=1 curl ... | bash`.

Prefere clonar: `git clone` + `./install.sh` faz o mesmo.
Passo a passo manual, sem script: [`INSTALAR.txt`](INSTALAR.txt).

### Por que Vesktop nativo

O daemon precisa do socket `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/discord-ipc-0`. O Discord em
Flatpak roda em sandbox com `/run` isolado e o socket não fica visível de fora.
Vesktop nativo (`.deb`/`.rpm`/pacote da distro) cria o socket no runtime dir
real do usuário — que é o que funciona.

---

## O ícone de bandeja

O menu é a interface inteira — não existe janela. Ele fala com o systemd, com
o arquivo de configuração e com o próprio catálogo do daemon.

| Menu | O que faz |
|---|---|
| **Daemon: running/stopped** | estado do serviço, no topo |
| **Detected now:** | o que está sendo detectado neste instante |
| **Apps Discord can see** | liga e desliga cada app do catálogo; marca com `• detected` o que está aberto agora |
| ↳ **Add a running app** | varre os processos abertos, cruza com a base de jogos detectáveis do Discord e adiciona o que reconhecer — em um clique, com o Application ID certo |
| ↳ **Remove an app I added** | tira do catálogo o que você adicionou |
| ↳ **Enable all / Disable all** | tudo de uma vez |
| **Appearance → Icon shape** | nove desenhos próprios: Blob, Controller, Broadcast, Bolt, Chat, Headset, Rocket, Ghost, Dot |
| **Appearance → Icon from desktop theme** | usa o ícone do tema do sistema (Breeze, no KDE): Discord, Vesktop, Games, Gamepad… — para o ícone combinar com o resto do painel |
| **Appearance → Color** | 15 cores com hex (paleta do Discord + Breeze/Plasma + neutras) e **Match KDE accent**, que lê a cor do seu esquema atual |
| **Daemon → Start at boot** | `systemctl --user enable` do daemon |
| **Daemon → Start tray at login** | o mesmo para a bandeja |
| **Daemon → Clear stuck presence** | manda o Discord apagar qualquer presença pendurada |
| **Daemon → Reload catalog / View log** | recarrega o catálogo; abre o journal em um terminal |
| **Configuration** | mostra o caminho do JSON, abre o arquivo, abre a pasta, copia o caminho |
| **Start/Stop/Restart daemon**, **Quit tray** | controle direto |

O ícone fica **acinzentado quando o daemon está parado** e colorido quando
está rodando, então dá para ver o estado sem abrir o menu. As preferências
ficam em `"tray"` dentro do mesmo `~/.config/discord-game-presence.json`.

Ele roda pelo serviço `discord-game-presence-tray.service`, ligado à sessão
gráfica. Para instalar sem a bandeja: `SKIP_TRAY=1 ./install.sh`.

---

## Adicionar seus próprios apps

Toda a configuração vive em `~/.config/discord-game-presence.json`. O que
estiver lá é aplicado por cima da tabela padrão: entradas novas são
adicionadas, entradas existentes têm só os campos citados trocados, e um
`client_id` vazio desliga a entrada.

### 1. Descubra o Application ID

Se o jogo estiver na base do Discord, use o id de lá:

```bash
curl -s https://discord.com/api/v9/applications/detectable \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys
for a in json.load(sys.stdin):
    if "parte do nome" in a["name"].lower(): print(a["id"], a["name"])'
```

Se **não** estiver (caso de Stremio, YouTube, e de qualquer app que não seja
jogo), crie um app seu em https://discord.com/developers/applications →
**New Application**. O nome do app é o nome que aparece no seu perfil. Suba
uma imagem em **General Information → App Icon** e copie o **Application ID**.

### 2. Descubra o processo

```bash
ps aux | grep -i <nome do app>
```

O casamento é por trecho da linha de comando, então qualquer parte estável
serve. É isso que permite pegar jogos sob Proton, cujo processo aparece como
`S:\common\Jogo\jogo.exe` — basta usar `jogo.exe`.

Comandos de shell (`bash -c …`) ficam de fora da busca de propósito: um
comando digitado no terminal carrega o próprio nome procurado e virava falso
positivo. Scripts de jogo (o `hl2.sh` do L4D2, por exemplo) continuam valendo.

### 3. Escreva a entrada

```json
{
  "games": {
    "jogo.exe": {
      "client_id": "1234567890",
      "details": "Nome do Jogo",
      "state": "Jogando",
      "large_text": "Nome do Jogo",
      "large_image": "https://exemplo/imagem.png"
    }
  }
}
```

| Campo | Para que serve |
|---|---|
| `client_id` | Application ID. Vazio desliga a entrada |
| `details` | primeira linha da presença |
| `state` | segunda linha |
| `large_text` | texto ao passar o mouse na imagem |
| `large_image` | nome de um Art Asset do app **ou** uma URL de imagem |
| `type` | `0` jogando, `2` ouvindo, `3` assistindo (veja os limites) |

Depois: `systemctl --user restart discord-game-presence`.

### Trocando os apps de mídia pelos seus

Stremio, YouTube e YouTube Music vêm apontando para apps que eu criei. Para
usar os seus (com o seu ícone), basta sobrescrever o id:

```json
{
  "games": {
    "youtube":                 { "client_id": "SEU_ID" },
    "youtube-music":           { "client_id": "SEU_ID" },
    "stremio":                 { "client_id": "SEU_ID" }
  }
}
```

### Quando o JSON não basta

Presenças que mudam sozinhas — servidor do Minecraft, mapa do L4D2, faixa
tocando — são funções Python na tabela `GAMES`, dentro do
`discord-game-presence.py`. `state` e `details` aceitam qualquer callable que
devolva texto; `state` pode devolver `(texto, extras)` para mandar também
`timestamps`, `buttons`, `party` ou trocar a imagem a cada faixa. Os detectores
existentes servem de modelo.

---

## Como as detecções mais interessantes funcionam

### Minecraft: servidor e lotação

1. acha o PID pela linha de comando (`PrismLauncher/instances`);
2. extrai a instância de `-Djava.library.path=.../instances/<nome>/natives`;
3. lista as conexões TCP com `ss -tnp`, descartando loopback e LAN;
4. resolve os hosts do `servers.dat` da instância e casa com o IP conectado —
   assim mostra `play.exemplo.com`, e não um IP de CDN;
5. faz um **Server List Ping** (handshake + status do protocolo Minecraft,
   ~30 linhas aqui) para pegar `online`/`max`;
6. publica como `party.size`, que o Discord escreve como "(860 of 5000)".

### Left 4 Dead 2: mapa

O L4D2 não expõe o mapa em processo, socket ou arquivo aberto — mapas oficiais
moram dentro de VPKs. A única fonte é o console. O instalador escreve
`con_logfile "console.log"` em `left4dead2/cfg/autoexec.cfg`, e o daemon lê o
fim do log, traduzindo `c2m3_coaster` → "Dark Carnival — capítulo 3".

> O log só passa a existir **depois de reiniciar o jogo** uma vez.

### GTA San Andreas: lendo o jogo por dentro

O jogo carrega em endereço fixo (`0x400000`, sem ASLR), então o estado sai de
`/proc/<pid>/mem`: ponteiro do jogador em `0xB6F5F0`, posição pela matriz da
entidade, vida em `+0x540`, dinheiro em `0xB7CE54`, veículo em `+0x58C`.

Os **nomes vêm do próprio jogo**, não de uma tabela embutida aqui: o
`data/info.zon` diz que zona cobre cada coordenada — vale a menor caixa que
contém o ponto, senão sai "Los Santos" no lugar de "Ganton" — e o
`text/american.gxt` traduz o código dela. O GXT indexa por **CRC32 invertido**
(JamCRC) do nome da chave, o que dá para confirmar testando contra chaves
conhecidas. O mesmo caminho nomeia os veículos, via `data/vehicles.ide`. Como
tudo sai dos arquivos do jogo, a presença acompanha o idioma instalado.

"Em missão" vem de `$ONMISSION`, a variável global `$26` do script. O endereço
não foi copiado da internet: `tools/gta-calibrar-missao.py` fotografa as
variáveis fora e dentro de uma missão e mostra quais foram de 0 para 1 — de
380 candidatos sobraram dois, e um deles é o `$26` conhecido.

Nada disso altera o jogo: só leitura.

# Proton Mirror

A Python script (invoked via a small Bash wrapper) that leverages the
[Proton Drive CLI](https://github.com/ProtonDriveApps/sdk/blob/main/cli/README.md)
to partially emulate `rclone sync`: synchronise the contents of two
directories, including deletion of files that no longer exist on the source.

Proton Drive CLI's built-in `upload`/`download` commands don't support
deletion, so this script fills that gap.

Run it via `./mirror.sh <pull|push> [options]` or `uv run mirror.py <pull|push>
[options]`; see `mirror.py --help` for the full command/flag reference.

## Prerequisites

- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) — dependencies are declared inline in
  `mirror.py` and resolved automatically by `uv run`.
- The `proton-drive` CLI must be installed, on `PATH`, and already
  authenticated (`proton-drive login` or equivalent) — this script only
  shells out to it and does nothing to set that up.
- `PROTON_MIRROR_LOCAL` must already exist as a directory before running
  either `pull` or `push` — it's never created for you.
- `PROTON_MIRROR_REMOTE` and `PROTON_MIRROR_LOCAL` both point
  directly at the folder being mirrored, not its parent — there's no extra
  nested folder inserted on either side.

## Pitfalls

- **An empty source is not a no-op.** `pull` from an empty
  `PROTON_MIRROR_REMOTE` still wipes everything in
  `PROTON_MIRROR_LOCAL` (and likewise `push` from an empty local folder
  wipes the remote) — an empty source means the *entire destination* is
  considered stale.
- **`pull` deletions are permanent.** They use `rm -rf`, not the trash.
  `push` deletions use `proton-drive filesystem trash` and are recoverable.
  Combine this with the point above: `pull --noconfirm` against an
  accidentally-empty or misconfigured `PROTON_MIRROR_REMOTE` will
  silently and permanently delete everything in `PROTON_MIRROR_LOCAL`
  with no chance to confirm. Double-check the remote path before using
  `--noconfirm` with `pull`.
- **`--dry-run` only previews deletions, not transfers.** `proton-drive`
  resolves upload/download conflicts internally, so there's no way to
  simulate what would actually be transferred or overwritten. The deletion
  list is the only concrete preview `--dry-run` gives you.
- A stale folder is reported and deleted as a single entry, not expanded
  into one entry per file inside it.

# bark × Proton Wallet — Route A prototype

A **real [bark](https://gitlab.com/ark-bitcoin/bark) wallet running on Bitcoin signet in
the browser**, wired into a Proton-Wallet-shaped UI. No server-side wallet, no daemon: the
bark WebAssembly bindings run in the page, talk to a live Ark server, and spend real signet
coins over Ark, Lightning and on-chain.

It exists to answer one question from a feasibility study: *can bark live inside Proton
Wallet's browser wallet, sharing a single seed?* This is **Route A** — bark keeps no
on-chain wallet of its own and borrows the wallet next to it.

## Run it with Claude Code

Paste this into Claude Code and it will do the rest:

```
Clone https://gitlab.com/matthewvuk/bark-proton-prototype and run it, then walk me
through funding it on signet and buying something from the Byte store.
```

The repo ships a `CLAUDE.md`, so any Claude Code session opened inside it already knows the
commands, the signet endpoints, the funding routes and the bark API traps.

## Run it by hand

Needs Node 20 or newer. Nothing else — no Rust toolchain, no bark daemon, no Bitcoin node.

```sh
git clone https://gitlab.com/matthewvuk/bark-proton-prototype.git
cd bark-proton-prototype
node server.mjs
```

Then open **http://localhost:5203/**. That is the whole setup — no `npm install`, because
the fork's WebAssembly is committed in `andromeda/` and the server has no dependencies.
Verified from a clean clone: it opens on signet, handshakes with the Ark server and hands
back a `tb1q…` address from andromeda's descriptor.

Two optional extras:

```sh
npm install && npm run dev     # adds the @secondts/bark comparison backend
```

`npm install` pulls the `@secondts/bark` bindings and `npm run dev` copies their WebAssembly
into `./bark/`. You only need this to click the backend pill over to *bark's own BDK* and
compare — Route A itself runs without it.

To rebuild the fork from source you do need Rust, `wasm-pack`, and **Homebrew LLVM**,
because Apple's `/usr/bin/clang` cannot target `wasm32` and `secp256k1-sys` will not
compile:

```sh
brew install llvm
cd andromeda-bark/crates/wasm
export CC=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar
export CC_wasm32_unknown_unknown=$CC AR_wasm32_unknown_unknown=$AR
wasm-pack build --target web --release --out-dir pkg-web
cp pkg-web/andromeda_wasm{.js,.d.ts,_bg.wasm} ../../../andromeda/
```

## What you get

A black bar across the top — deliberately WordPress-shaped, so it is obviously not part of
any product — carrying three pages and one switch.

| Tab | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Info** | Route A explained: the derivation problem, the architecture, the key ceremony, what is proven and what is not |
| **Demo** | The wallet: both balances, both coin sets (UTXOs and VTXOs), Send, Receive, Board, Offboard, history |
| **Store** | Buy a real item from Second's signet store, paid out of the Ark balance over Lightning |

Next to those tabs is a second control that matters more than it looks: a pill naming
**which wallet backend is live**, which you click to swap. It is the difference Route A is
about, and you can see it in one field — the on-chain receive address:

| Backend | On-chain derivation | Address it hands you |
|---|---|---|
| **andromeda BDK** (default) | `m/84'/1'/0'` — andromeda's account | `tb1qwukcfvaftfgkt5l3dwt7ga86dtv9nhj9ps6yus` |
| **bark's own BDK** | `m/86'/1'/0'` — bark's own wallet | `tb1p7puw9swfjjqk566h4wp85kyy3hl2z9war4n7ghay0dpz0ftlhfqskl762f` |

Same seed, same page, same Ark identity. One gives you a BIP-84 segwit address because
bark is spending **andromeda's** BDK wallet through the adapter; the other gives a BIP-86
taproot address because bark brought its own. That `tb1q` versus `tb1p` is Route A working,
and it is the single most useful thing to show someone.

The **Ark layer** switch turns the Ark surfaces on and off, and its state follows you
between tabs. Off, you see a single on-chain balance. On, it splits into two labelled
layers — on-chain and instant — and you get both coin lists side by side: the **UTXOs** the
BDK wallet holds, and the **VTXOs** the Ark layer holds on top of it, with **Board** and
**Offboard** to move value between them.

## The one manual step: funding

A fresh wallet is empty, and an empty wallet cannot pay for anything. Open **Receive** on
the Demo tab to read this browser's addresses — each browser profile gets its own wallet —
then pick either route:

1. **Ark, directly.** Second's faucet at `signet.2nd.dev` can send to the `tark1…`
   address. It asks for a GitHub sign-in (the faucet does; the store does not). Fastest.
2. **On-chain, then board.** Any public signet faucet pays the `tb1p…` address. Once it
   confirms, hit **Board into Ark**. This is the more interesting path, because boarding
   *is* the mechanism Route A is about: the on-chain wallet funds the board, and bark takes
   the resulting VTXO.

## What is in this repository

Four things that fit together. Two are code we wrote, two are open-source code we build on.

```
                    ONE SEED (12 words)
                            │
        ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐
        │                                       │
   THE RUST PATH                          THE BROWSER PATH
   the real Route A                       what you can run right now
        │                                       │
   andromeda-bark/                         wallet.js
   Proton's Rust core,                     plain ES module
   with bark compiled in                        │
        │                                       │
        │  crates/wasm/src/ark/                 │  @secondts/bark  (npm)
        │  ├── mod.rs      wiring               │  bark's published
        │  ├── onchain.rs  THE ADAPTER          │  WebAssembly build
        │  └── api.rs      20 JS exports        │
        │                                       │
        ▼                                       ▼
   bark spends ANDROMEDA'S                 bark spends ITS OWN
   BDK wallet                              BDK wallet
        │                                       │
        ▼                                       ▼
   built into a 27.7 MB wasm               runs in the page today,
   bundle -> WebClients                    live on signet
        │                                       │
        └──────────────┬────────────────────────┘
                       ▼
                   proton/
        Proton Wallet's real front end,
        which both paths render inside
```

**The difference between the two paths is the whole study,** so it is worth being exact:

| | `andromeda-bark/` (Rust) | `wallet.js` (browser) |
|---|---|---|
| Whose BDK wallet does bark spend? | **andromeda's** | bark's own |
| How many on-chain wallets exist? | **one** | two, disjoint |
| Runs from a clone? | needs a wasm build | **yes** |
| Proves | Route A is implementable | Route A's design works end to end |

The browser path is honest about being a stand-in: bark's published npm package exposes
only its own `OnchainWallet`, so a plain page cannot borrow andromeda's. Closing that gap is
the upstream ask at the bottom of this README.

## How the pieces connect

Two Rust crates, one seed, one BDK wallet. The adapter in the middle is the whole idea.

```
  ┌─ andromeda-bark/  (the fork, GPL-3.0, source in this repo) ─────────────┐
  │                                                                        │
  │   bark::Wallet                        andromeda::Account               │
  │   Ark: rounds, VTXOs, arkoor,         BDK, BIP-84, m/84'/1'/0'         │
  │   exits, Lightning                    the only UTXO set that exists     │
  │        │                                       ▲                       │
  │        │ needs an on-chain wallet              │ IS that wallet        │
  │        ▼                                       │                       │
  │   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────┐                │
  │   │  ProtonOnchain : bark::onchain::OnchainWalletTrait │                │
  │   │  balance · address · sync · is_mine · register_tx  │                │
  │   │  prepare_tx · prepare_drain_tx · finish_psbt       │                │
  │   │  make_signed_p2a_cpfp · store_signed_p2a_cpfp      │                │
  │   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                │
  │        onchain.rs, 755 lines. this is Route A.                          │
  │                                                                        │
  │   crates/wasm/src/ark/api.rs  — the 22-call JS surface:                 │
  │   open_wallet board offboard send_arkoor send_onchain vtxos balances    │
  │   history sync refresh tip ark_address onchain_address start_exit       │
  │   pay_invoice bolt11_invoice claim_lightning_receives  (added here)     │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        │  wasm-pack build --target web
                        ▼
              andromeda/andromeda_wasm.js  +  _bg.wasm   (26 MB, committed)
                        │
        ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
        │                               │
        ▼                               ▼
  THIS repo's page               Proton's own React app
  wallet.js picks a backend      packages/wasm/andromeda/ swapped
  backend-andromeda.js  ◄── the  for this bundle; no component
  same wasm, loaded by a         is modified. see integration/
  plain <script type=module>
```

The left branch is what you run here. The right branch is what Proton would ship, and the
reason the bundle is built `--target web` as well as `--target bundler`: the same Rust,
reachable from a plain page or from their webpack build.

### The two backends, side by side

`wallet.js` is a selector, not an implementation. Both files behind it export the same
names, so no page knows which is live:

```
                        wallet.js  (selector, ?backend=…)
                              │
              ┌───────────────┴────────────────┐
              ▼                                ▼
  backend-andromeda.js               backend-bark.js
  the fork, --target web             npm @secondts/bark
                                      
  bark ──┐                           bark ──► its own BDK wallet
         ├─► ProtonOnchain ──┐               (BIP-86, m/86'/1'/0')
         │                   ▼                        │
         │        andromeda::Account            ┌─────┴──────┐
         │        (BIP-84, m/84'/1'/0')         │ two wallets │
         └────────────────┬──────────────────┐  │ one seed    │
                          ▼                  │  └────────────┘
                  ONE BDK wallet              │
                  ONE UTXO set                └── the before-picture
                  ── Route A ──
```

Route A is the left one. The right one is kept on purpose: it is what the problem looks
like before the adapter, and it is the only backend that does LNURL and Lightning
addresses, because those types live in `lnurllib` and bark does not re-export them.

`integration/` records the WebClients side: the one `package.json` change, and how the
bundle is swapped. No React component is modified — which is the claim, and also the limit.

# GE-Proton Updater

A Bash script to automatically download, verify, and install the latest [GE-Proton](https://github.com/GloriousEggroll/proton-ge-custom) ([GloriousEggroll](https://x.com/GloriousEggroll)'s excellent Proton fork) for Steam on Linux desktops / laptops. Keeps your gaming compatibility tools up-to-date with minimal hassle.

- **Standalone**: Runs anywhere to update GE-Proton.
- **Hook-Friendly**: Perfect as a post-update script for [apt-up](https://github.com/cwadge/apt-up) or [pac-up](https://github.com/cwadge/pac-up). Fully dry-run aware via `IS_DRY_RUN`.
- **Efficient**: Nothing happens unless it needs to.
- **No Restart Required**: After initial setup, GE-Proton updates are picked up by Steam automatically — no restart needed.

## Features
- Fetches the latest GE-Proton from GitHub.
- **Architecture-aware**: auto-detects the host CPU (`x86_64` or `aarch64`) and downloads the matching GE-Proton build. Since GE-Proton11-1, upstream ships both, and the script selects the correct asset for your machine.
- Verifies checksums for security and consistency.
- Installs to a **static** `GE-Proton-Latest` directory in `~/.steam/steam/compatibilitytools.d` (or a custom path), with a customized `compatibilitytool.vdf` so Steam recognizes it as **"Proton GE Latest"**.
- Automatically rotates the previous version to `GE-Proton-Previous` (**"Proton GE Previous"**) as a fallback in case of critical bugs.
- After initial setup, **no Steam restart is required** for updates — the static internal name means Steam uses the new build immediately.
- Tracks installed versions via a state file (`.ge-proton-version`) to avoid redundant downloads.
- Cleans up legacy versioned directories (e.g. `GE-Proton10-27`) from older script versions.
- Handles user ownership (no root-owned files in your home dir).
- Skips root installs as accidental unless explicitly allowed (`--force-root`).
- **Dry-run aware**: checks `IS_DRY_RUN` when run as a hook and reports what would happen without downloading or installing anything.
- Debug mode for troubleshooting (`--debug`).

## How It Works
Instead of extracting each GE-Proton release to its own versioned directory (e.g. `GE-Proton10-30`), this script uses **static directory names** with rewritten `compatibilitytool.vdf` files:

| Directory | Internal Name | Display Name (in Steam) |
|---|---|---|
| `GE-Proton-Latest/` | `GE-Proton-Latest` | `Proton GE Latest` |
| `GE-Proton-Previous/` | `GE-Proton-Previous` | `Proton GE Previous` |

Since Steam's `CompatToolMapping` in `config.vdf` references tools by their **internal name**, keeping the internal name static means you only need to select `Proton GE Latest` once. After that, every update transparently replaces the contents of that directory and Steam uses the new build at the next game launch.

The actual GE-Proton version installed under each slot is tracked internally via a `.ge-proton-version` state file and reported in the script's output.

## Prerequisites
- `Bash`, `curl`, `tar`, `sha512sum` (standard on most distros).
- `Steam` installed natively (`.deb`, package manager, etc.).
- A supported CPU architecture: **x86_64** (amd64) or **aarch64** (arm64). The script auto-detects yours and fetches the matching build. You can force a specific build with `GE_PROTON_ARCH` (see Usage) — handy under a translation layer (FEX-Emu, box64, qemu-user) or to stage a build for another machine. An unrecognized CPU falls back to x86_64 with a warning rather than failing.

> **Flatpak Steam users**: This script is not compatible with Flatpak Steam. Upstream GE-Proton tarballs include pressure-vessel, which cannot nest inside Flatpak's sandbox. Install GE-Proton via Flatpak instead:
> ```bash
> flatpak install com.valvesoftware.Steam.CompatibilityTool.Proton-GE
> ```

## Example Run
Here it's found a new version, rotated the previous Latest to Previous, downloaded and checksummed the new release, extracted it, and rewrote the VDF files:
```
Checking for GE-Proton updates...
Using overridden Steam directory: /home/chris/.steam/steam/compatibilitytools.d
Latest version: GE-Proton10-30
Rotating GE-Proton-Latest (GE-Proton10-29) → GE-Proton-Previous...
Previous version: GE-Proton10-29
Downloading GE-Proton10-30.tar.gz...
/tmp/ge-proton-update.BJfprL/GE-Proton10-30.tar.gz          100% 478.83M 90.1MB/s in 5.2s
Verifying checksum...
Checksum verification passed
Extracting GE-Proton10-30 to /home/chris/.steam/steam/compatibilitytools.d/GE-Proton-Latest as user chris...
GE-Proton10-30 installed as 'Proton GE Latest'!
==> Updated in-place. No Steam restart required.
Done!
```

## Installation
### Standalone
```bash
curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cwadge/ge-proton-updater/main/ge-proton-updater -o /usr/local/bin/ge-proton-updater
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/ge-proton-updater
ge-proton-updater
```

### As an `apt-up`/`pac-up` Hook
1. Copy to the `apt-up` post-hook directory:
```bash
sudo curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cwadge/ge-proton-updater/main/ge-proton-updater -o /etc/apt-up.d/post.d/50-ge-proton
sudo chmod +x /etc/apt-up.d/post.d/50-ge-proton
```

Or for `pac-up`:
```bash
sudo curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cwadge/ge-proton-updater/main/ge-proton-updater -o /etc/pac-up.d/post.d/50-ge-proton
sudo chmod +x /etc/pac-up.d/post.d/50-ge-proton
```
2. (Optional) Set a custom target in `/etc/apt-up.conf` or `/etc/pac-up.conf`:
```bash
EXPORT_VARS="GE_PROTON_TARGET=/home/youruser/.steam/steam/compatibilitytools.d"
```

3. Run `sudo apt-up` or `sudo pac-up`.

### Dry-Run Awareness

When installed as an apt-up or pac-up hook, the script automatically respects dry-run mode. Both parent scripts export `IS_DRY_RUN=true` before running any hooks when `--dry-run` is active. The updater checks this variable and, if set, queries the GitHub API for the latest version and reports what it would do — without downloading, extracting, or modifying anything:

```
[DRY-RUN] Would update GE-Proton: GE-Proton10-29 → GE-Proton10-30
```

or, if already up to date:

```
GE-Proton10-30 is already up to date.
```

No special configuration is needed — dry-run awareness is built in.

## Usage
- **Standalone:** `ge-proton-updater` (updates for the current user).

- **Root with Custom Target:** `GE_PROTON_TARGET=/path/to/dir sudo ge-proton-updater`.

- **Force Root Install:** `ge-proton-updater --force-root` (if you're running Steam as root for some wild and unforeseen reason).

- **Force Architecture:** `GE_PROTON_ARCH=aarch64 ge-proton-updater` (or `x86_64`) — overrides CPU auto-detection and fetches that build regardless of the host. Useful when running x86_64 GE-Proton under a translation layer on ARM (or vice versa), or to stage a build for a different machine. Accepts `x86_64`/`amd64` and `aarch64`/`arm64`; an unrecognized value is treated as an error.

- **Dry-Run:** `ge-proton-updater --dry-run` — checks for a newer version and reports what would happen without downloading or modifying anything.

- **Debug Mode:** Something going wrong? Run `ge-proton-updater --debug` for full verbiage.

## Steam Setup
After the **first** GE-Proton install, Steam needs to be told to use it:

1. Restart Steam.

2. Go to `Steam` > `Settings` > `Compatibility`.

3. Set "Default compatibility tool:" to `Proton GE Latest`.

**That's it — you only need to do this once.** Future updates will be picked up automatically without restarting Steam.

If a new build causes issues, you can switch to `Proton GE Previous` as a fallback until the next release.

## Migrating from Older Versions
If you were previously using versioned directory names (e.g. `GE-Proton10-27`, `GE-Proton10-28`), the script will:

1. Install the latest version to `GE-Proton-Latest/` with the new static naming.
2. Automatically clean up any legacy versioned directories.

After migrating, you'll need to restart Steam once and select `Proton GE Latest` as your compatibility tool. From that point forward, updates are seamless.

## Multi-User, Multi-Steam Systems
For systems with multiple Steam users, adapt the script as follows:

### Admin And Gamer Aren't The Same User:
1. Set `GE_PROTON_TARGET` upstream for the gamer's Steam path,
e.g. edit `/etc/apt-up.conf` or `/etc/pac-up.conf`:
```bash
EXPORT_VARS="IGNORE_CC_MISMATCH=1 GE_PROTON_TARGET=/home/gamer/.steam/steam/compatibilitytools.d"
```

2. Run `sudo apt-up` or `sudo pac-up`.

### Standalone, Multiple Gamers:
Run the script once per user with `GE_PROTON_TARGET` as a CLI variable:
```bash
GE_PROTON_TARGET=/home/gamer1/.steam/steam/compatibilitytools.d ge-proton-updater
GE_PROTON_TARGET=/home/gamer2/.steam/steam/compatibilitytools.d ge-proton-updater
...
```

### Called By A Hook In An Update Script, Multiple Gamers:
Use multiple copies of the script with hard-coded targets:

1. Copy and edit the script for each user:
```bash
sudo cp ge-proton-updater /etc/apt-up.d/post.d/ge-proton-updater-gamer1
sudo chmod +x /etc/apt-up.d/post.d/ge-proton-updater-gamer1
# Edit ge-proton-updater-gamer1, uncomment and set: GE_PROTON_TARGET="/home/gamer1/.steam/steam/compatibilitytools.d"
sudo cp ge-proton-updater /etc/apt-up.d/post.d/ge-proton-updater-gamer2
sudo chmod +x /etc/apt-up.d/post.d/ge-proton-updater-gamer2
# Edit ge-proton-updater-gamer2, uncomment and set: GE_PROTON_TARGET="/home/gamer2/.steam/steam/compatibilitytools.d"
...
```

2. Run parent script, e.g. `sudo apt-up` or `sudo pac-up`. Each hook updates its respective user's GE-Proton individually.

    - Be sure you don't set `GE_PROTON_TARGET` in `apt-up.conf`/`pac-up.conf` in this case, as it'd override the script-specific targets.

# Enhanced Virtual Surround Sound for Focusrite Scarlett 16i16 4th Gen

**STATUS: PRODUCTION-READY ✅**

A professional-grade virtual surround sound solution for the Focusrite Scarlett 16i16 4th Gen interface on Arch Linux with PipeWire. Creates virtual 5.1 and 7.1.4 surround sound sinks that properly downmix to your 4-channel speaker setup using ITU-R BS.775 compliant algorithms. A bundled configurator (`python -m configurator`) generates equivalent configs for other pro-audio interfaces and speaker layouts.

**Performance**: 23-25ms total latency - excellent for professional recording, mixing, and production work.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Install the configuration
cd working-solution/
./install-enhanced-surround.sh

# Test the system
../diagnostic-tools/universal-channel-tester.py

# Verify installation
wpctl status | grep enhanced_virtual
```

## Key Features

✅ **ITU-R BS.775 Compliant Downmix** - Professional audio industry standards  
✅ **Proper Center Channel Positioning** - Center content appears from front speakers only  
✅ **Enhanced 7.1.4 Support** - Optimized height channel distribution  
✅ **Robust Implementation** - Uses only proven PipeWire filter types  
✅ **Universal Testing** - Auto-discovery via PipeWire API  
✅ **DAW Integration** - Compatible with Harrison Mixbus Immersive Mix  
✅ **Generic Configurator** - Generate configs for any interface and speaker layout (`python -m configurator`)  

## System Requirements

- **OS**: Arch Linux (or compatible)
- **Audio System**: PipeWire 1.4.6 or later
- **Hardware**: Focusrite Scarlett 16i16 4th Gen
- **Speakers**: 4-channel setup connected to AUX0-AUX3
- **Desktop**: KDE Plasma (recommended for audio settings)

## Enhanced Channel Matrix

### 5.1 Surround Downmix
```
FL_out = FL + 0.707×FC + 0.4×LFE
FR_out = FR + 0.707×FC + 0.4×LFE
RL_out = RL
RR_out = RR
```

### 7.1.4 Surround Downmix
```
FL_out = FL + 0.8×FC + 0.25×LFE + 0.6×TFL
FR_out = FR + 0.8×FC + 0.25×LFE + 0.6×TFR
RL_out = RL + 0.9×SL + 0.7×TRL
RR_out = RR + 0.9×SR + 0.7×TRR
```

## Wine/Proton Game Compatibility

### The Problem
Wine/Proton games crash or experience severe audio distortion when directly connecting to virtual sinks with auxiliary (AUX0-AUX3) channel labels. This is due to Wine's inability to handle non-standard channel configurations.

### The Solution (CONFIRMED WORKING)
Use game-compatible virtual sinks with standard FL/FR/RL/RR channel labels:

```bash
# For maximum compatibility (RECOMMENDED - works with all games)
PULSE_SINK=enhanced_virtual_51_gamecompat %command%

# For 7.1.4 capable games (game-dependent, test first)
PULSE_SINK=experimental_virtual_714_bassmanaged %command%
```

**7.1.4 Compatibility**: Game-dependent! Some games work perfectly (Helldivers 2), others crash (Arc Raiders). Start with 5.1 for universal compatibility. The 7.1.4 sink uses standard channel labels just like the 5.1 game-compat one, plus routes bass to a real sub at AUX16.

### Installation
Game-compatible configs are production-ready:
```bash
# 5.1 (production, hand-written):
~/.config/pipewire/pipewire.conf.d/enhanced-5.1-game-compatible.conf

# 7.1.4 + sub (configurator-generated; see documentation/EXPERIMENTAL-SINKS.md):
~/.config/pipewire/pipewire.conf.d/experimental-7.1.4-bass-managed.conf
```

### Benefits
- ✅ **Full surround preserved** (5.1 or 7.1.4) - NOT stereo fallback
- ✅ **Zero distortion** - proper channel recognition
- ✅ **Universal 5.1 compatibility** - works with all tested games
- ✅ **7.1.4 for capable games** - Helldivers 2 confirmed working
- ✅ **Priority settings** - automatic proper device selection

## Usage

### KDE Desktop Integration

1. Open KDE System Settings → Audio
2. Enable "Show virtual devices"
3. Select either:
   - **Virtual 5.1 Surround on Scarlett 16i16**
   - **Virtual 7.1.4 Surround on Scarlett 16i16**
4. Set as default output device

### DAW Integration

#### Harrison Mixbus Immersive Mix
The Virtual 7.1.4 Surround on Scarlett 16i16 sink is fully compatible with Mixbus Immersive Mix 7.1.4 output. See `documentation/MIXBUS-CHANNEL-MAPPING.md` for detailed channel routing.

### Wine/Proton Gaming

For Windows games via Wine or Steam Proton:

```bash
# Steam/Proton - 5.1 (universal compatibility)
PULSE_SINK=enhanced_virtual_51_gamecompat %command%

# Steam/Proton - 7.1.4 (test per-game, works with Helldivers 2)
PULSE_SINK=experimental_virtual_714_bassmanaged %command%

# Standalone Wine applications
PULSE_SINK=enhanced_virtual_51_gamecompat wine game.exe
```

**Important Notes:**
- ✅ **5.1 works universally** - all games tested (Fallout 4, Sulfur, Arc Raiders)
- ⚠️ **7.1.4 is game-dependent** - works with Helldivers 2, crashes Arc Raiders
- Start with 5.1, test 7.1.4 per-game if you want full height channels
- Game-compatible configs use FL/FR/RL/RR labels instead of AUX channels
- Full surround audio preserved (NOT stereo fallback)

### Testing and Validation

```bash
# Universal channel testing with auto-discovery
./diagnostic-tools/universal-channel-tester.py

# System diagnostic analysis
./diagnostic-tools/analyze.sh

# Verify channel mapping
./diagnostic-tools/diagnose-channel-mapping.sh
```

## Physical Speaker Layout

The system is optimized for speakers positioned **behind** the listener (not to the sides):

```
    FL ---- FR
    |        |
    |  YOU   |
    |        |
    RL ---- RR
```

**Key Benefits:**
- **7.1.4 virtual sink** treats rear speakers as truly behind you
- **Side content (SL/SR)** routes to rear speakers with proper spatial mapping
- **Height channels** provide additional immersive positioning
- **Better surround field** than 5.1 for content with distinct side/rear channels
